exposure: vaginal delivery after a previous cesarean section (VBAC)
cohort: 85,428 women who delivered vaginally over a 10-year period at a single tertiary medical center
finding: Women undergoing their first vaginal delivery after a previous cesarean section were not at increased risk for obstetric anal sphincter injury compared with primiparous women.
mod_finding: This study found that secundiparous women who underwent vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) did not have an increased risk for obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) compared with primiparous women.
